subject.title: feat(process): add starvation guard to priority command queue

question: Should command lanes guarantee eventual service for normal work under a sustained foreground stream, or should fresh foreground retain strict precedence even when that permits normal work to starve?
rationale: The proposed cap intentionally preserves foreground precedence, while the linked issue explicitly asks for a starvation guard; code cannot satisfy both guarantees without an approved fairness policy or bounded-service rule.

options.title: Define bounded fairness
options.body: Specify a foreground burst budget, age threshold, or other bounded-service rule so normal work eventually runs, then update the selector and regression tests.

options.title: Keep strict foreground precedence
options.body: Accept that normal work may remain queued during sustained foreground traffic, narrow the PR and linked issue language so it no longer promises starvation prevention.

options.title: Defer scheduler aging
options.body: Keep the existing static-priority behavior until the broader queue fairness policy has an approved owner and acceptance criteria.

recommendation.title: Define bounded fairness
recommendation.body: Specify a foreground burst budget, age threshold, or other bounded-service rule so normal work eventually runs, then update the selector and regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the merged command-queue priority model whose fairness semantics this PR extends.
